ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text:
The situations of four small cars moving from the same place in the same direction are respectively shown in the figures below. Which of the following statements is correct?
A. Car A moves in a straight line, and car B moves in a curved line
B. All four cars start moving from rest
C. During the time from 0 to $t_{2}$, cars C and D are farthest apart at time t2
D. During the time from 0 to $t_{2}$, the distance between cars C and D first increases and then decreases

ready2_open_rewrite.resolved_question_text: As shown in the figure, four small cars move from the same place in the same direction. During the time from 0 to t2, when are cars C and D farthest apart?
ready2_open_rewrite.resolved_answer: During the time from 0 to t2, cars C and D are farthest apart at time t2
ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: First describe the graph: on the right is the velocity-time graph of cars C and D, the vertical axis is v/(m·s^-1), and the horizontal axis is t/s. C corresponds to the straight line starting from the origin, and D corresponds to the curve starting from the origin and gradually becoming gentler; during the time from 0 to t2, D's curve is above C's straight line, and the two lines intersect at t2. Then reason: in a velocity-time graph, the higher the curve is at the same time, the greater the velocity is. Therefore, during 0～t2, the velocity of car D is greater than or equal to that of car C, and for most of the time the velocity of car D is greater than that of car C. The stem states that the two cars move from the same place in the same direction, so the distance between the two cars starts from 0; because D is always faster than C, the distance between C and D continuously increases with time. Thus, in this time interval, being farthest apart occurs at the terminal time t2.
